{{more footnotes|date=February 2025}}
In [[mathematics]], especially [[algebraic topology]] and [[homotopy theory]], the '''Hopf–Whitney theorem''' is a result relating the [[homotopy classes]] between a [[CW complex]] and a multiply connected space with [[singular cohomology]] classes of the former with coefficients in the first nontrivial [[homotopy group]] of the latter. It can for example be used to calculate [[Cohomotopy set|cohomotopy]] as [[Sphere|spheres]] are multiply connected.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hopf |first=Heinz |date=1933-12-01 |title=Die Klassen der Abbildungen dern-dimensionalen Polyeder auf dien-dimensionale Sphäre |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01297505 |journal=Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici |language=de |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=39–54 |doi=10.1007/BF01297505 |issn=1420-8946|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Statement ==
For a <math>n</math>-dimensional [[CW complex]] <math>X</math> and a <math>n-1</math>-[[connected space]] <math>Y</math>, the well-defined map:

: <math>
[X,Y]\rightarrow H^n(X,\pi_n(Y)),
[f]\mapsto f^*\iota
</math>

with a certain [[cohomology class]] <math>\iota\in H^n(Y,\pi_n(Y))</math> is an [[isomorphism]].

The [[Hurewicz theorem]] claims that the well-defined map <math>\pi_n(Y)\rightarrow H_n(Y,\mathbb{Z}),[f]\mapsto f_*[S^n]</math> with a [[fundamental class]] <math>[S^n]\in H_n(S^n,\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}</math> is an isomorphism and that <math>H_{n-1}(Y,\mathbb{Z})\cong 1</math>, which implies <math>\operatorname{Ext}_\mathbb{Z}^1(H_{n-1}(Y,\mathbb{Z}),\pi_n(Y))\cong 1</math> for the [[Ext functor]]. The [[Universal coefficient theorem]] then simplifies and claims:

: <math>
H^n(Y,\pi_n(Y))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbb{Z}(H_n(Y,\mathbb{Z}),\pi_n(Y))
\cong\operatorname{End}_\mathbb{Z}(\pi_n(Y)).
</math>

<math>\iota\in H^n(Y,\pi_n(Y))</math> is then the cohomology class corresponding to the [[Identity map|identity]] <math>\operatorname{id}
\in\operatorname{End}_\mathbb{Z}(\pi_n(Y))</math>.

In the [[Postnikov tower]] removing [[Homotopy group|homotopy groups]] from above, the space <math>Y_n</math> only has a single nontrivial homotopy group <math>\pi_n(Y_n)\cong\pi_n(Y)</math> and hence is an [[Eilenberg–MacLane space]] <math>K(\pi_n(Y),n)</math> (up to [[weak homotopy equivalence]]), which classifies [[singular cohomology]]. Combined with the canonical map <math>Y\rightarrow Y_n\simeq K(\pi_n(Y),n)</math>, the map from the Hopf–Whitney theorem can alternatively be expressed as a postcomposition:

: <math>
[X,Y]\rightarrow[X,K(\pi_n(Y),n)]\cong H^n(X,\pi_n(Y)).
</math>

== Examples ==
For homotopy groups, cohomotopy sets or cohomology, the Hopf–Whitney theorem reproduces known results but weaker:

* For every <math>n-1</math>-connected space <math>Y</math> one has:

: <math>
[S^n,Y]
\cong H^n(S^n,\pi_n(Y))
\cong\pi_n(Y).
</math>
: In general, this holds for every topological space by definition.

* For a <math>n</math>-dimensional CW complex <math>X</math> one has:

: <math>
[X,S^n]
\cong H^n(X,\pi_n(S^n))
\cong H^n(X,\mathbb{Z}).
</math>
: For <math>n=1</math>, this also follows from <math>S^1\simeq K(\mathbb{Z},1)</math>.

* For a [[topological group]] <math>G</math> and a [[natural number]] <math>n</math>, the Eilenberg–MacLane space <math>K(G,n)</math> is <math>n-1</math>-connected by construction, hence for every <math>n-1</math>-dimensional CW-complex <math>X</math> one has:

: <math>
[X,K(G,n)]
\cong H^n\left(X,\pi_nK(G,n)\right)
\cong H^n(X,G)
</math>
: In general, this holds for every [[topological space]]. The Hopf–Whitney theorem produces a weaker result because the fact that the higher homotopy groups of an Eilenberg–MacLane space also vanish does not enter.
